result.title: VariaFlow: Uncertainty-Aware Flow Matching for Unsupervised Anomaly Detection
result.summary: Reconstruction-based anomaly detection no longer fails at reconstruction. Generative models produce high-quality pseudo-healthy reconstructions, and the remaining difficulty is the step of scoring residuals. The residual between a scan and its reconstruction has two indistinguishable sources, genuine pathology and the anatomical variation that separates one healthy brain from another. Scoring against a single reconstruction treats both as anomalous, inflating false positives where healthy anatomy varies most while small or subtle lesions are lost in the surrounding reconstruction error. We identify the missing quantity as the predictive variance, how much a healthy reconstruction can vary at each location. We introduce VariaFlow, which estimates this variance from an ensemble of mask-guided restorations under an unconditional flow matching prior, each started from a different noise initialization, and which normalizes the residual by the resulting standard deviation. Few-step flow matching keeps the ensemble computationally affordable, and restoring at two spatial scales captures lesions of different size. Across three brain MRI datasets spanning stroke and tumor, VariaFlow is trained once on healthy anatomy and generalizes across all three, attaining the highest AUROC (0.94, 0.80, 0.78) on each and the highest AUPRC on both cross-domain datasets, exceeding the strongest baseline by 37% and 50%. Under domain shift, the same baseline drops by up to 52% in AUPRC, whereas VariaFlow stays more stable and achieves the best small-lesion Dice on all three datasets.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 VariaFlow：在无条件 flow matching 先验下用不同噪声初始化做掩码引导修复集成，估计每个位置的预测方差，并用其标准化重建残差，从而区分真实病变与正常解剖变异，在三个脑 MRI 数据集上做无监督异常检测。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「集成估计预测方差、再按不确定性归一化残差」的机制可能可供核查：在 LVR 中或可用于区分任务必要的视觉证据与无关变异，并为视觉细节的可信度筛选与停止决策提供不确定度信号。
